links.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid reading grade level of chatbot glaucoma responses versus AAO brochures
links.effect: Readability levels for AAO, ChatGPT, Bing, and Bard were 8.11, 13.01, 11.73, and 7.90; ChatGPT and Bing were above AAO (p<0.0001).
links.quote: AAO information and Bard responses were at the most accessible readability levels (AAO versus ChatGPT, AAO versus Bing, Bard versus ChatGPT, Bard versus Bing, all p<0.0001), with readability levels for AAO, ChatGPT, Bing, and Bard at 8.11, 13.01, 11.73, and 7.90, respectively.

links.outcome: Readability of chatbot patient-education responses relative to patient comprehension levels
links.effect: ChatGPT and Bing responses were at FKGL 13.01 and 11.73, above AAO brochures at 8.11; Bard was 7.90.
links.quote: With accuracy scores and comprehensiveness below that of AAO brochures and elevated readability levels, AI chatbots require improvements to be a more useful supplementary source of glaucoma information for patients.

screen.reason: Evaluates commercial LLM chatbots (ChatGPT-4, Bard, Bing) on patient education questions regarding glaucoma compared to AAO brochures, without testing a specific implementation safeguard or deployment practice.
